provenance: OPS-SAT-AD (Ruszczak et al., 'The OPS-SAT benchmark for detecting anomalies in satellite telemetry', Scientific Data 12, 2025; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12588359, CC BY 4.0). Real telemetry from ESA's OPS-SAT CubeSat, which reentered in May 2024. These are the 19 precomputed per-segment features of the benchmark's own TEST partition, entire and unsampled, so the figure below is the one the dataset's 30 published baselines are quoted against. Not comparable with the Telemanom model on this same page: that one forecasts continuous ESA-ADB series, this one classifies pre-segmented fragments.
split: the benchmark's own test partition, whole: a stratified random split, not a temporal one
attribution: Ruszczak, Kotowski, Evans & Nalepa, 'The OPS-SAT benchmark for detecting anomalies in satellite telemetry', Scientific Data 12, 710 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41597-025-05035-3, CC BY 4.0. Data: Ruszczak, B., Kotowski, K., Nalepa, J. & Evans, D., 'OPSSAT-AD - anomaly detection dataset for satellite telemetry', Zenodo (2024), doi:10.5281/zenodo.12588359 (version 1).
modifications: The 19 published per-segment features of the benchmark's test partition, all 529 segments, rounded to 6 decimals, with the published labels.

expected.note: The whole published test split, so this reproduces the benchmark's own partition rather than a resample of it. The accuracy above is the exported ONNX graph's own on these rows, which carry the partition's values to float32 precision, the precision the graph reads. Until Round 86 they were rounded to 6 decimals, which flipped 8 decisions, and this note blamed the export for the gap; the export reproduces the scikit-learn model on these rows.
